deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's 1983-84 notes on systems (arrangements) of pseudo-lines. The page is numbered 10 in his own pagination. Throughout, D and D' are pseudo-line configurations. Σ is presumably a fixed combinatorial type or ambient situation, and Γ(Σ) is a graph or complex whose vertices are configurations and whose arrows D→D' are 'specialisations'. A specialisation contracts a triangular cell T of D to a triple point, which is the elementary degeneration in a triangle flip (Ringel move); the reverse direction is a generalisation. To each configuration he attaches a combinatorial polygon Pol(D), with variants Pol'(D) and Pol(D)*. Its edges are labelled by 'triangles (arêtes) de spécialisation', i.e. the triangular cells of D whose contraction gives a specialisation. Its edges also carry integer weights ('pondérations').

(1) Left column, top. He studies how weights transfer along a specialisation D→D'. Vertices and edges of Pol'(D) and Pol(D') correspond to each other. The exceptions are the singular vertices and the two edges α, β that cut the edge γ, which are not yet weighted. The 'formule des pondérations' then forces, for the corresponding edges α', β' of Pol(D'), the additivity relation poids(α') + poids(β') + poids(ω) = poids(γ). He first wrote and struck out a version with α''. So the weight of the edge γ that is destroyed or split is redistributed over the new edges plus a residual edge ω. This is a local conservation law for the weights under one flip or degeneration step.

(2) Left column, NB. He proposes to regard Pol(D) or Pol(D)* as augmented by 'free' edges. These correspond to the specialisations, and more importantly the antispecialisations, of D or D' within Γ(Σ). They are drawn as half-edges ('arête ... avec une origine, mais pas d'extrémité'). Seen from Γ(Σ), such vertices look like free (smooth) edge-ends. The specialisation arrow D→D' then induces an isomorphism P^α(D) → P^α(D') on the relevant part.

(3) Right column. He corrects the earlier reasoning in terms of P(D)→P(D'). When a triangle T is affected by specialisation, the one or two specialisation triangles adjacent to T can disappear as such. Hence the adjacency relation between the specialisation triangles of D must be recorded as part of the structure Γ(Σ). A margin NB says this adjacency is deducible from the structure of the weights. To get the extra structure, one first removes from Pol(D) the specialisation triangles adjacent to T, giving a smaller polygon Pol(D,T̂). Then one 'augments' Pol(D) by free edges standing for 'pseudo-triangles de spécialisation'.

The next page completes this. Pol*(D) is the polygon enlarged by antispecialisations as free edges. The specialisation induces an embedding Pol*(D) → Pol*(D') that is only an isomorphism onto a sub-polygon. It fails to be onto because new triangles or pseudo-triangles are created when a face adjacent to T, or a lateral face, is a quadrilateral. This is the standard fact that flipping T changes the side-counts of neighbouring faces by ±1.

Purpose: to build a functorial local combinatorial invariant of a pseudo-line configuration. It should be compatible with specialisation and flips, and should make Γ(Σ) into a richer, 2-dimensional or stratified, combinatorial object recording which flips are available and how they interact.
errors: No outright error is visible, but the argument is fragmentary. The 'formule des pondérations' is invoked without being stated on this page. Pol(D) is never defined here, so the additivity poids(α')+poids(β')+poids(ω)=poids(γ) cannot be checked independently.

Grothendieck himself flags a gap in his earlier reasoning ('Les réflexions en termes de P(D)→P(D') ...'). That reasoning ignored that triangles adjacent to T can stop being triangles under the specialisation. The next page adds the converse: triangles can also be created when an adjacent face is a quadrilateral. So a naive 'iso' P(D)≅P(D') is false in general and only holds on the part P^α.

ideas.what: Specialisation D→D' of pseudo-line configurations (contracting a triangular cell to a triple point), organised into a graph or complex Γ(Σ)
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flips / Ringel moves; the flip graph of pseudoline arrangements; the stratification of the space of arrangements (cf. higher Bruhat order B(n,2))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for connectivity under flips; Goodman–Pollack (1980s); Manin–Schechtman (1986-89) for higher Bruhat orders; Felsner–Weil and others for the flip graph
ideas.where_published: Only in the Montpellier archive notes on pseudo-lines (cotes around 154)

ideas.what: Integer weights on the edges of the polygon Pol(D), with an additivity law under specialisation: w(α')+w(β')+w(ω)=w(γ)
ideas.modern_name: No standard name; resembles conservation laws for face or cell counts under flips, or multiplicity data on cells of a stratification

ideas.what: Adjacency relation between flippable triangles recorded as extra structure on the flip graph, making it 2-dimensional
ideas.modern_name: 2-cells of the flip complex (commuting flips giving squares; polygonal relations around higher-multiplicity points); higher Bruhat orders / Kapranov–Voevodsky's 2-categorical structure on braid-like moves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Manin–Schechtman (1989); Kapranov–Voevodsky (1991); Ziegler (1993, higher Bruhat orders and oriented matroids)

ideas.what: Free half-edges ('antispécialisations', edges with an origin but no end) added to Pol(D) to get Pol*(D), so that specialisation induces an embedding of polygons
ideas.modern_name: Augmented star or link of a cell in a stratified space; boundary half-edges in a ribbon-graph-like encoding

ideas.what: Flipping a triangle T changes neighbouring triangles: adjacent triangles may disappear, and new ones appear when an adjacent face is a quadrilateral
ideas.modern_name: Elementary face-size change under a triangle flip

missed.claim: Around 1983-84, independently, Grothendieck was building local polygons attached to arrangements, with functoriality under specialisation and recorded adjacency of flippable triangles. This makes the flip graph into a richer structured complex, essentially the combinatorics that Manin–Schechtman (higher Bruhat orders, 1986-89) and Kapranov–Voevodsky later formalised. The link to that literature is not recorded.
missed.quote: il faudrait donc indiquer la relation d'adjacence des triangles de spécialisation de D, comme faisant partie de la structure Γ(Σ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a priority and historical data point: Grothendieck approached the 2-dimensional structure of the space of pseudo-line arrangements from a geometric 'specialisation/stratification' viewpoint, before the higher-Bruhat literature.

missed.claim: A weight system ('pondérations') on Pol(D) satisfying an additivity law under specialisation is proposed, and claimed to determine the triangle-adjacency structure. It is never fully defined or proved here.
missed.quote: poids(α') + poids(β') + poids(ω) = poids(γ) ... NB elle est déduite de la structure des pondérations
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: If reconstructible from the surrounding pages, it might give a numerical invariant of arrangements that controls flip adjacency. That would be of possible interest for flip-graph combinatorics. On this page alone it is too fragmentary to judge.

deep.surprise_reason: These are working notes developing a combinatorial device (weighted polygons, free antispecialisation edges, triangle adjacency) for the flip or specialisation structure of pseudo-line arrangements. The ideas parallel later higher-Bruhat and flip-complex work and are unpublished. But the page is fragmentary, the central objects are not defined on it, and the facts actually stated are elementary flip combinatorics.
transcription_corrections: 'La formule des pondérations implique dans quoi doit avoir' should probably read 'implique donc qu'on doit avoir'.
'Je ne connais d'arguments la polygone' is likely something like 'Je ne considère d'ailleurs le polygone Pol(D), ou Pol(D)*, ... regardés'; the transcription is garbled.
'avec H sommets' is probably 'avec ses sommets' or similar.
'ou "anti-points"' is more likely 'ou "antispécialisations"', consistent with the next page.
'pas d'extrémité) - dans un regard pas d'extrémité) - dans un regards' is a duplicated line; the image has it once.
'on argumentera Pol(D)' should be 'on augmentera Pol(D)', consistent with Pol*(D) being 'plus grand' on the next page.
'Les réflexions en termes de P(D)→P(D') et mouvements' is likely 'Les réflexions en termes de P(D)→P(D') sont incomplètes / sont mauvaises ...'; it introduces a self-correction.
'Pol(D, T̂)' reads as Pol(D) with the adjacent triangles of T removed; the image shows a hat-like mark over T.
The margin note near the bottom left ('pris et ... plus ...') is illegible in the transcription; it seems to read something like 'peut-être ... plus simple'.
